According to the latest issue of the "Power On" newsletter, Apple reportedly once considered adding a feature to its "Apple Upgrade" programme that would make the process of switching to a new iPhone almost seamless: user data would be transferred in advance before the new device ships. However, this feature was never actually implemented.

The concept is quite simple: if users regularly upgrade their devices through a fixed monthly instalment plan, why not make the transition as convenient as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported:

There are some obvious loopholes here. First, your iCloud backup will be slightly outdated, because data can only be transferred at the moment of shipment, which is a few days after the order is placed, unless you choose to pick up the device in person at a store.

Apart from that, there are also obvious privacy concerns. That said, if you have always been using iCloud backup, it is no surprise that Apple has your data. But the average user may worry about how the data is transferred to the new phone, and whether anyone has had access to it during the process.

Two years ago, Apple fully rolled out a brand-new system called "Presto" across its retail stores, which allows store staff to update the software while the iPhone is still in its box. It is not hard to imagine extending this system in the future to support iCloud backup transfer, without anyone touching your data throughout the process.

However, this feature was ultimately not brought to market — and this may actually be a good thing.
